About 10 European flights were targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday, forcing the brief closure of a Warsaw airport and the scrambling of air force planes in Rome, authorities said. No explosives were found, despite extensive searches on the ground after the planes all took off and landed safely in different European cities just several hours apart. Irish budget carrier Ryanair appeared to be the worst hit, with four of its flights to different destinations being targeted. London’s Metropolitan police confirmed it “was made aware of threats… against four aircraft due to depart from or arrive at Heathrow Airport” Tuesday, one of Europe’s busiest air hubs. It gave no further details, but also said there was a further warning about a flight at Manchester Airport. Following checks “no security issues were identified”, the Met police added. Aena, the Spanish airport operator, confirmed an emergency protocol was activated “due to a bomb alert” on a Ryanair flight which landed at 10:30 am (0930 GMT) from Manchester at Murcia in southeastern Spain. The plane arrived without problems. Other Ryanair flights from Lisbon to Rome, Dublin to Rome, and Dublin to the Bulgarian capital of Sofia also received warnings. Italian air force jets were scrambled to escort Ryanair flight FR9611 from Dublin as it landed at Rome-Fiumicino at 10:45 am (0945 GMT), Rome Airport said in a statement. Anti-bomb procedures were also put in place when an earlier Ryanair flight arrived at 9:40 am (0840 GMT) at the airport. “Checks on passengers, luggage and the plane were all negative and the alert was lifted,” the statement added. The incidents all come after fighter jets were scrambled on Monday when a Wizz Air flight from London’s Luton airport to Sofia was diverted following a bomb threat and forced to make an emergency stop in Budapest. – Airport briefly shut – Scandinavian Airlines said it could “confirm that a threat has been made against flight SK751 between Copenhagen and Warsaw”, but the plane landed Tuesday without any problem. It arrived at Warsaw’s Chopin airport, which closed one runway as the plane underwent a security inspection, but no explosives were found. The LOT flight, which had also been scheduled to arrive at Chopin, was diverted to the Polish capital’s other airport, Warsaw Modlin. Authorities closed that airport following the alert, but the Boeing 737 MAX also landed safely. “Nothing was found,” Modlin airport spokesman Adam Szablowski told AFP. Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said on Facebook that on Monday NATO’s air defence alert service had issued an alert for a Wizz Air flight from London’s Luton. “The Hungarian Defence Forces’ Gripen fighter jets took to the air within minutes and ensured the safe landing of the passenger aircraft in Budapest,” he said.
